name: brownfield
requirement: Marketing needs to shorten many URLs at once from a spreadsheet. Add a batch endpoint to the existing URL shortener that accepts up to 50 URLs in one request. Either all links are created or none: a single invalid URL must reject the whole batch and tell the caller which entries were wrong.
constraints:
Existing codebase: url-shortener-service (Java 21, Spring Boot 3.5, Gradle Kotlin DSL, package io.github.hemanthvk980.shortener).
Follow its conventions: layering api → service → repo → domain (enforced by ArchUnit), RFC 7807 errors via common.GlobalExceptionHandler,
configuration via AppProperties. Only modify files under url-shortener-service/. Tests: JUnit 5 + MockMvc in the existing style.

design: APPROVED: all-or-nothing is what marketing asked for; reuse of create() keeps behaviour identical
review: APPROVED: risk accepted for the internal marketing rollout; follow-up ticket SHORT-142 weights rate-limit tokens by batch size before public exposure
release-readiness: APPROVED: additive, backward-compatible API change; ship
